problem: Split floors one shared total/sum(weights) and distributes leftover units round-robin instead of by largest remainder, so results are not proportional (allocate('10',[1,100]) gives [0.55, 9.45] vs main's [0.10, 9.90]; ~60% of random cases differ from main).
_ref.allocate(...) consumes a one-shot iterator passed as weights, so line 20 sees an empty sequence and raises ZeroDivisionError (main accepted generators).
Leftover loop can iterate about total_units times instead of at most len(weights), so large amounts with large weights take seconds (3.7 s for allocate('1000000',[10**9,10**9])).

Production module imports reference_impl, calls its private _to_decimal, and runs the full allocation twice only for validation, leaving the local _to_decimal dead and making any oracle comparison tautological.
No tests exist and none would catch the F1 regression; equal-weight cases pass on both versions, so unequal weights with remainders are needed.
Commit 'allocate: rework the implementation' lacks a conventional-commit type and the branch name 'review-candidate' does not match the naming pattern.
